change: Initial spec
Weight as power family plays^alpha; added raw-capped and hit-indicator return metrics; continuous-parameter sweep policy
why: Robert asked about log/exponent transforms and continuous vs discrete parameters

change: Benchmark peers = other users' bets in the same month x popularity bin (all computed leave-one-out), rather than "random artists of that popularity"
why: Clarification while implementing: makes leave-one-out symmetric for the bet and its peers; excess return = how your bets did vs everyone else's comparable bets

change: Weeks map to months by their midpoint; market observed only to 2012-12
why: Implementation detail; data thin out in 2013

change: Durability (C): artists not found on ListenBrainz count as 0 listeners (main); dropping them is a variant
why: 12% of artists missing, almost all tiny (30% of 1-4-listener artists, 0.4% of 5000+), so missing ~ never listened

change: Scenes: co-listening clusters partly encode *when* artists got popular (scene explains 10-29% of variance in artists' peak year; e.g. Skrillex, Gotye, Foster the People grouped — all 2011 breakouts). Proposed: genre-based scenes (MusicBrainz genres; 86% of plays covered, but only 9-18% of small artists) with untagged artists assigned by their listeners' earlier listening; current clusters kept as a contrast
why: Within-scene benchmarks would otherwise compare breakouts to breakouts and hide foresight

change: Scenes: year-by-year co-listening, 200 scenes (main) (each year's relatedness uses only earlier listening; artists existing before the year keep their pre-period co-listening position, new/small artists are placed by their listeners' earlier taste). Variants: 50 / 1000 scenes; all-years co-listening and genre-tag scenes as contrasts. Replaces the genre-tag proposal above
why: Robert preferred relatedness (co-listening) over labels; the actual problem was using future listening. Chosen on taste-independent quality criteria (analysis/out/scene_quality.txt): relatedness lift 9.0x vs 8.5x for the leaky all-years version (which was even fitted in-sample), with ~half the timing leak (0.11 vs 0.20); genre tags cover only 57% of bets. A first version had one catch-all scene holding 20-63% of listening (popular artists' diverse audiences average to a generic point) — fixed before comparison. Bets in 2005 have no scene (no earlier data)

change: Added momentum control: benchmark cells also by quintile of the artist's prior 6-month fixed-panel growth (leave-one-out). Artist-age cells (months since first listened; pre-2005 artists censored as one group) implemented as already specified
why: Standard factor control from finance (Carhart momentum) that should have been in the spec: adopting artists that are already rising earns returns without foresight. Together with scene and age controls, tests whether the primary signal is "style exposure" rather than skill

change: Controls (scene, age, momentum) applied additively (main): month x popularity-bin cells, then leave-one-out month x scene / month x age / month x momentum adjustments, backfitted. Fully crossed cells kept as a contrast only
why: Crossing all controls made cells tiny (8 artists per cell; 26% of bets in cells with a single artist), so bets were compared mostly to other people adopting the *same* artist, which mechanically erases artist-choice signal (persistence 0.13 crossed vs 0.23 additive). Each run now reports cell diagnostics

change: Model B uses taste communities instead of each user's k nearest neighbours: a user's community in year Y = users sharing their home scene, the scene they are most over-represented in during the previous 12 months (share of their plays / everyone's share, among scenes with >= 5% of their plays). Outcome = ln((later community adopters + 0.5) / community members active throughout); always adjusted additively for the artist's prior popularity within the community (deciles)
why: k-NN over 297k users x 36M bets (~7B lookups) was impractical. A first version used plain argmax of plays and put most users into a few big mainstream scenes (bet-weighted mean community ~26k users vs ~1.5k intended), so communities reflected popularity rather than taste; fixed before any B results

change: Variants with ~2-8x more bets (no onboarding cutoff, 2-week commitment, every first listen) run on a random half of users (hash), compared against the main controlled version on the same half
why: They exceed the machine's memory/disk budget at full size; half the users (~120k scored) is ample for persistence estimates

change: Model B also adjusted (additively) for month x community: the community's overall adoption rate that month
why: First B run showed very high persistence (0.33 across separate periods) that the impostors explained more of after controls (R^2 0.08 -> 0.21) — consistent with B rewarding membership in communities that adopt a lot, a stable trait of where you sit rather than foresight. B's outcome counts later adopters in *your* community, so the community's own rate must be the benchmark. Earlier B results kept as model_B/*_v1_no_community_fx

change: Evaluation framework adopted (EVALUATION.md): 12 construct x unit candidates, one pipeline, one scorecard (forward prediction first; luck, impostors and 3-year stability as gates; reliability, robustness, coverage), bootstrap intervals, pre-declared selection rules. Step-2 numbers are superseded by the pipeline's
why: Robert: the goal is the *best* model with every decision justified; step 2 evaluated candidates piecemeal

change: Persistence measured as a year-by-year stability curve (lags 1-5, corrected for yearly measurement noise; lags shorter than the horizon flagged), plus the forward test with a gap of horizon/12 + 1 years
why: Robert: two fixed periods were arbitrary

change: Scene-level bets: one bet per scene a person newly enters (no earlier committed artist there, < 5% of plays in it the previous year), dated at the first committed artist, judged by the scene's growth; each scene counts once. Scene universes per year; later artists mapped to the most-overlapping scene
why: Robert questioned whether removing "being in a growing scene" is fair; scene picking becomes its own candidate instead of only a control

change: Song-level bettors = raw-sample users (1/8): dating a song commitment needs weekly listening, stored only for them. Song popularity = new listeners (first plays) in the trailing 6 months within the fixed panel; song age replaces artist age; no song momentum control
why: Data limitation

change: Discernment: compared with artists/songs/scenes with the same prior track record of keeping triers (analogue of popularity for prescience). Community-leading (artist): also adjusted for momentum *within the community*. Song/scene community-leading: share of your community adopting/entering after you, adjusted for the community's monthly rate
why: Weak spots identified in step 2 (EVALUATION.md §5)

change: New control: release timing (album/EP/single released in the 3 months before, after, both, neither, or no data; MusicBrainz release groups). New impostor: the person's own commitment rate (loyal listener)
why: "Is it just following music news?" and "is it just being a loyal listener?"

change: Impostors: replaced the 10% impostor-share gate with incremental validity. Headline = forward prediction after removing impostors (residualized); rank by it; gate = its interval excludes zero; impostor share reported, not gated. Planned: impostor features from the past period only
why: Small-sample tests: durability (10.6% share) kept only 38% of its prediction after adjustment while community-leading (11.6%) kept 78%. A share cutoff is arbitrary and misclassifies; incremental validity is the standard approach

change: Song unit: songs by the same artist adopted in the same month are collapsed into one bet (mean excess); split halves by artist
why: First song scorecards showed implausible reliability (0.88-0.98) and luck shares (up to 0.96): a person's song bets cluster by artist/album and move together, so per-song split halves and per-song luck shuffles treated correlated bets as independent. Same logic as scene bets counting each scene once. Superseded scorecards kept in analysis/out/cand/_superseded/

change: Song unit: finer song-age control (months since first appearance 0 / 1 / 2 / 3-5 / 6-11 / 12-23 / 24+, previously one group for < 3 months)
why: After collapsing, community-leading for songs still showed implausible reliability (0.91) and luck share (0.93); likely "following new releases": songs gain most listeners right after release, so release-day listeners see many later community adopters without foresight

change: Community-leading for songs and scenes now also compared with songs/scenes equally popular *within the bettor's community* beforehand (deciles, additive), as the artist version already was
why: Omission found in the "is it just X" table: song-level community-leading barely moved when any control was removed (0.31 throughout), consistent with crediting picks already popular among similar people

change: Freeze: Confirmation section written and committed before any sealed-half analysis
why: Robert approved FREEZE_MEMO recommendations, with a primary *family* (discernment at three levels) instead of a single primary model, and Holm correction within families (instead of a flat 99.6%)

change: Sealed-run pre-check (explore rerun reproduces the explore result) uses a tolerance of 0.001 instead of exact equality
why: First attempt stopped on a 1e-5 difference from non-deterministic tie-breaking in popularity bins and parallel floating-point sums; the headline's uncertainty is ~0.005. Implementation check only; frozen plan unchanged

change: Song unit: weight variants now apply to merged song bets (weight from the merged bet's total early plays)
why: Bug: merging same-artist songs set every bet's weight to 1, so the weight sweeps for songs were no-ops (main settings use equal weights, so frozen results are unaffected)

change: Individual percentile range (descriptive, write-up only) now uses the true-score formula: mean sqrt(reliability) x z, SD sqrt(1 - reliability)
why: The earlier formula (mean reliability x z, SD sqrt(1 - reliability^2)) gave the range of a fresh sample of picks, not of the true standing: discernment-songs 75th percentile was shown as 31st-92nd, correct is about 42nd-90th. Not part of any confirmation rule
